newsitem.title: USA: Excerpts from O.J. Simpson's testimony.
newsitem.headline: Excerpts from O.J. Simpson's testimony.

text.p: The following are excerpts from O.J. Simpson's testimony at his wrongful death civil trial Monday.
On wanting to commit suicide on June 17, 1994, the day he was due to surrender to police and five days after the murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend Ronald Goldman:
"I was feeling a lot of pain...I just wanted to go to Nicole's grave. I was feeling, I guess, suicidal. I just wanted my pain to end.

"I was in a lot of pain. I was missing Nicole. My kids didn't cry. I guess they had attacked me somewhat and that hurt me and I guess I just didn't know what to do," Simpson said. It was not clear who he was referring to when he said "they."
On why he didn't kill himself:
"Partially A.C. (Cowlings, his best friend), and my mother told me years ago that you didn't go to heaven if you committed suicide."
On his conversation with Los Angeles police from his Chicago hotel room after being told Nicole Brown Simpson was dead:

"The first thing I was told was that my kids were alright but they were in a police station and that concerned me. I wanted to know if my kids had been exposed to anything and he (Det. Ron Phillips) said 'no,' that they had been taken out the back (of Nicole Brown Simpson's condominium) and they didn't see anything."
(Nicole Brown Simpson and Goldman were stabbed and slashed to death on the front walkway of the condominium.)
On his interview with two Los Angeles police detectives the day after the murders:
"I didn't care if they talked to me or not. I needed a lawyer.
"I was tired, I was in shock, I was disbelieving, I was a lot of things."
On whether he had anything to hide:
On a conversation he had with Nicole's mother, Juditha Brown, during a wake for Nicole.
"She asked me if I had anything to do with it. She really got right up in my face, and I said, no, I didn't. I loved your daughter."
On an argument he got into with a golfing buddy on the day of the murders:
"I told him on no uncertain terms that he was sort of a butthole."
